passages.provision_quote: Sec. 8. (a) Except as provided in subsection (b), a governmental entity may not substantially burden a person's exercise of religion, SEA 101 — Concur 3 even if the burden results from a rule of general applicability. (b) A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Enacted text of SB 101 creates a strict-scrutiny exemption standard a person may invoke against any governmental burden on religious exercise.
House Roll Call 305 on 3rd reading/final passage of SB 101 lists Soliday among the Yea votes.

rows.reasoning: Soliday voted Yea on final passage of SB 101 (2015) (Roll Call 305, Yea 63-Nay 31), a single-subject enrolled act whose operative text requires government to show a compelling interest and least restrictive means before substantially burdening a person's exercise of religion, creating an enforceable exemption. This matches 'protect religious freedom and allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs,' while excluding rung 5 (the strict-scrutiny test is a limit, not complete autonomy) and rung 3 (the act creates an enforceable exemption right, not mere balance language).
